intro.text: When you look up the word “law” in a dictionary, you’ll typically find more than 20 different definitions, but they do break down into two main categories: 1) made-up rules that require enforcement (e.g., tax laws), and 2) principles or protocols upon which reality is constructed to operate (e.g., laws of physics).

definition.text: In order for a law to be a design law, it must be a principle or protocol upon which reality operates. As such it will be testable — with reproducible, consistent, constant, and predictable results. In other words, it is non-changing.

constantine.text: Human beings did not and cannot create reality as God did; instead, when we make up rules, we must enforce those rules externally, most often through the infliction of punishment. Sadly, after Constantine “converted,” the idea that God’s law functions in the same way that human laws do was embraced; the idea that God’s law is imposed (imperial) began to infect Christianity — corrupting the saving truths that Jesus brought.

laws.name: The law of love
laws.text: the principle of giving upon which life is built to operate; examples:
examples: We give CO2 to the plants, and they give oxygen to us
The water cycle (oceans > clouds > rain > rivers > oceans)
Plants give pollen to bees and bees their industry to pollinate the plants

laws.name: The law of liberty
laws.text: Love only exists in the atmosphere of freedom. Violate freedoms in relationships and three predictable and damaging consequences will occur:
consequences: Love is damaged and eventually destroyed
Rebellion (desire to break away and get free) is incited
Individuality of the one dominated will be eroded and eventually destroyed if the violations do not end

laws.name: The law of worship
laws.text: We are changed neurobiologically and characterologically to become like what we admire, worship, and spend time watching and assimilating.

laws.name: The law of exertion
laws.text: Strength comes from exercise — “use it or lose it” — not just physically, but also neurologically.

laws.name: The laws of physics
laws.text: law of gravity, friction, motion, nuclear forces, etc.

laws.name: The laws of mathematics
laws.text: such as commutative laws, a + b = b + a, etc.

laws.name: The laws of health
laws.text: the physical laws upon which life and health operate, including nutrition, exercise, sleep, hydration, respiration, etc.

laws.name: The law of restoration
laws.text: After expending a resource, one must rest and recover before one is enabled to expend more. For example, a baseball pitcher must rest and recover before he can pitch again, lest he cause permanent damage to his arm.

laws.name: The law of sowing and reaping
laws.text: We reap what we sow — not just in fields, but in life. One cannot get grapes by sowing oats, and we cannot get critical reasoning skills by allowing others to think for us. For example, simply getting the correct answers from a textbook or teacher, rather than figuring out those answers ourselves. This is why the Bible says that the mature are those who have trained their faculties by practice to be able to discern right from wrong (Hebrews 5:14).

laws.name: The law of love overcoming fear
laws.text: Genuine love overcomes our fear for self and allows us to sacrifice self for others. Neurobiologically, when our love circuit fires, it calms our fear circuit. For example, a mother who sees her child in danger puts herself in harm’s way to save the child, but she would not put herself in such danger on her own whim.

laws.name: The law of fear damaging love and inciting selfishness
laws.text: When our fear circuits are active and we identify with them and focus on the fear, we lose concern for others, think of self, and neglect or harm others, in order to protect or save self. Consider being in a theater during a mass shooting: If we don’t know anyone else, the fear drives concern for self and most people seek only to escape the danger, maybe even pushing others out of the way to get out. But if you are with a loved one, you don’t simply flee; you seek to save your loved one, perhaps even putting yourself between the shooter and the one you love.

laws.name: The law of forgiveness versus resentment
laws.text: When wronged, we can either forgive or not. When we forgive, we free ourselves from bitterness and resentment and experience healing of our heart and mind, but retaining resentment always injures us. We cannot experience emotional and mental wellness while harboring bitterness.

laws.name: The law of truth
laws.text: You can never avoid the truth; you can only delay the day you deal with it.
detail: When truth is embraced and accepted, it displaces lies and frees a person from fear and misunderstanding, elevating and ennobling the individual. Truths build together into beliefs, constructs, and perspectives that form our understanding of reality, leading us back to trust in our Creator God. In trust, we open our hearts and experience the indwelling Spirit of God that transforms and ennobles us to be beings of love rather than beings of selfishness. All truth comes from God and, if followed, will lead back to God.

When truth is rejected, our understanding is confused, our mind is damaged, our heart is hardened, and we slowly become less capable of understanding reality — the truth of God’s kingdom and the world around us. Such individuals will one day face the truth, but it will be painful and destructive to them as they still hate the truth and want to flee from it, even begging for the mountains and rocks to hide them from reality (Luke 23:30).

laws.name: The law of revelation
laws.text: People reveal or bring forth and share what they truly believe and value. Those who value God’s principles not only speak them, but live them. Conversely, those who love the methods of this sinful world live them out. Thus, Jesus said, “Out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks. The good man brings good things out of the good stored up in him, and the evil man brings evil things out of the evil stored up in him” (Matthew 12:34, 35).

laws.name: The law of happiness
laws.text: Happiness is the byproduct of healthiness in all domains — physical, mental, emotional, relational, and spiritual. One only experiences happiness when in harmony with God’s design laws upon which these aspects are built. Break the laws of health and sickness, disease, and suffering occur — thus undermining happiness. Many people fail to understand this and instead of pursuing healthiness, they substitute pleasure seeking, which often violates the laws of health (e.g., drugs, alcohol, casual sex, gambling, etc.) and only causes greater unhappiness.

laws.name: The law of brokenness
laws.text: Once there is brokenness (injury) of any kind, there are no pain-free options. Do nothing and one remains in pain and disabled. But healing and recovery from brokenness is painful. Sadly, many fail to realize this when it comes to emotional wounds and, rather than facing the pain and healing the injury, they spend their lives seeking pain relief, rather than healing. But in so doing, they never get well and only get worse, because once there is brokenness, there are no pain-free options. The first step to healing is to embrace this truth and stop asking, “What hurts least?” and start asking, “What is the best action to take to heal, even if it hurts?”

laws.name: The law of sin and death
laws.text: This is also known as survival of the fittest, the principle of fear-driven selfishness that infects the world. This is Satan’s law — the strong dominate and exploit the weak. It is the violation of the law of love and liberty, and it also has predictable results: pain, suffering, and eventually death.

closing.text: God is our loving Creator who built all reality to operate in harmony with His character of love. His laws are design laws, protocols upon which life and health are constructed to operate.

reuse_note.text: The seventeen law definitions are reused from the Two Lenses page, where they were fact-checked against Jennings' 2019 post.

intro.text: Jennings calls liberty the atmosphere love breathes. Take freedom out of a relationship and three things follow as predictably as a dropped stone falls: love dies, rebellion stirs, and if the person stays, their very selfhood thins to a shadow. The widget below lets you run his 'spouse test' as a thought experiment and then meet the real patients he describes.

statement.text: I described for the first time the law of liberty, the principle of freedom upon which God created reality to operate. I described how this law is, like gravity, a constant that works whether one believes in it or not and that just like gravity, it is testable – there are reproducible and unavoidable consequences when we violate liberty.
statement.speaker: Jennings

statement.text: Violate liberty, and love is always damaged. Eventually it will even be destroyed. A desire to rebel is instilled in the heart, but if one surrenders to violations long enough, individuality is shattered so that only a shadow remains. Love cannot exist in an atmosphere without freedom. This law is not enacted or legislated; it is one of the principles on which life is designed to operate, and our health and happiness are dependent on harmony with it.
statement.speaker: Jennings

quote.text: Whenever liberty is violated, three predictable consequences occur: (1) love is always damaged and will eventually be destroyed;
quote.speaker: Jennings

quote.text: (2) a desire to rebel is instilled in the heart
quote.speaker: Jennings

quote.text: if one has the option to restore freedom but instead chooses to remain violated, then (3) individuality is slowly eroded and the person becomes, like Joe, a mere shadow.
quote.speaker: Jennings

spouse_test.text: Test it on your significant other. For a day, try restricting his or her liberties. Tell your special other where he can go, what she must wear, when he can use the phone, how much money can be spent. See for yourself what happens to love. … Conversely, if you are in a relationship in which freedoms have been abused, begin to breathe in liberty and see if love revives.
spouse_test.speaker: Jennings

quote.text: So Joe began to limit his activities. He stopped volunteering and stopped meeting with friends. Over the years he withdrew more and more in order to please his wife, in order to keep her happy. In public he stopped socializing. He no longer initiated conversations. When someone asked him a question, he looked to his wife for permission to speak. Slowly, gradually, almost imperceptibly Joe faded away. He lost himself.
quote.speaker: Jennings

what_was_controlled.text: His time, his friendships, his volunteering, even permission to speak in public — surrendered to keep an unhappy, jealous wife calm.

consequence.text: Forty years on he is a 'shadow': no initiative, no conversation, looking to his wife before answering a question. Individuality eroded.

quote.text: Lynda told me she had married a man who was domineering, controlling and demanding. He monitored her every move. He gave her money only to use as he directed. When money was given for groceries, her husband required that she give him receipts showing every penny spent and returning any change to him. She could not use the phone without permission, and was forbidden from talking to old friends or developing new ones. … She was being suffocated as a person.
quote.speaker: Jennings

what_was_controlled.text: Money to the penny (receipts and change returned), the phone, every friendship, every move.

consequence.text: Panic attacks, depression, suicidal hospitalisations, fourteen failed medications — the mind fighting for air before it goes under for good.

quote.text: Hesitantly she described one incident in which her husband told her he wanted dinner ready at 5:00 p.m., and how she had worked diligently preparing the meal, but served it at 5:02 p.m. She cried as she told how her husband began to beat her, breaking her nose and blackening her eye. … “Oh no! It wasn’t his fault. If I would have had dinner ready on time, he wouldn’t have had to hit me.”
quote.speaker: Jennings

what_was_controlled.text: Her body and her schedule, enforced by beatings framed as love ('I only do this for your own good').

consequence.text: Stage three: she defends her abuser and blames herself. Her own judgement has been replaced by his version of reality.

god_respects.text: God will never violate his own character of love, which means God does not take away freedom or operate contrary to the law of liberty.
god_respects.speaker: Jennings

god_respects.text: God’s laws are not like the laws of creatures; God does not govern by made-up rules enforced through coercion and externally inflicted penalties, because such methods violate liberty, damage love, incite rebellion, and destroy individuality.
god_respects.speaker: Jennings

intro.text: For Jennings the law of love is not a sentiment but the operating principle of every living system: a circle of giving. Oceans give to clouds, lungs give carbon dioxide to plants, plants give oxygen back. Trace the circle in the widget, then break it and watch what happens.

circle.text: The oceans give their waters to the clouds, which rain over the land, giving their waters to form the lakes, rivers and streams, which in turn give their waters to the plants and animals, ultimately giving back to the oceans to start the circle again.
circle.speaker: Jennings

circle.text: We see the circle of love, the law of life, in everything God creates. In every breath we demonstrate giving: we give away carbon dioxide to the plants, and the plants give back oxygen to us.
circle.speaker: Jennings

circle.text: This design—this law of giving—is the foundation of every living system: the water cycle, pollination, citric-acid cycle, nitrogen cycle (plant growth, digestion of plants, fertilization), economies, ecosystems, literally everything that lives—gives. And everything that doesn't give—dies!
circle.speaker: Jennings

broken.text: If a body of water separates from the circle and ceases to flow, it stagnates and everything in it dies. God gave us a powerful illustration in the body of water called the Dead Sea. The Dead Sea takes from the Jordan River but gives nothing in return. What happens in that body of water? The name says it all.
broken.speaker: Jennings

broken.text: Imagine if you were to decide, "I don't want to be a part of the circle of giving. If my body makes carbon dioxide, it's mine; I have the right to it. You can't have it." The only way to do that is to stop breathing—to die. If we hoard the product of our breathing, maybe by putting a bag over our heads, the carbon dioxide becomes the poisoning agent that kills us.
broken.speaker: Jennings

survival.text: Fear and selfishness are commonly known in the world today as "survival of the fittest," or the drive to survive, or "kill or be killed," or "watch out for me first." It is the polar opposite of giving, love or beneficence, and it is the infection that is destroying God's creation.
survival.speaker: Jennings

In all my actions, I demonstrated to you how to live in harmony with God's design for life–the law of love. By hard work, we support the weak, remembering the truth the Lord Jesus taught: 'It is a greater blessing to give than to receive.' "

Life is constructed to operate upon giving, so give; and the more you give, the more will be given to you: a great abundance of love — concentrated, intense, overwhelming and all-consuming — will be poured into your being. For the way you treat others reveals the condition of your own character, and your own condition determines your destiny."

intro.text: Strength comes by exercise — muscles, skills, reasoning, faith. Jennings reads the parable of the talents as a lesson in this design law: what you use grows, what you neglect withers. Slide the 'use' dial below and watch the capacity respond.

statement.text: Law of exertion: strength comes by exercise. If you want something to get stronger, you must exercise it. If you don't use it, you will lose it.
statement.speaker: Jennings

statement.text: If you want something to grow stronger, you must exercise it; as everyone knows, if you don't use it, you lose it. If you don't exercise a muscle group, an ability, or a talent, it will slowly wither away.
statement.speaker: Jennings

examples.text: When a person exercises their abilities, those abilities grow stronger. Those with musical talent who take lessons and practice, athletes who train, mathematicians who pursue higher education and challenge their thinking, artisans—craftsmen of every kind who exercise their craft grow stronger, more capable, and more proficient. Those with raw talent who neglect it will over time lose the ability they have, while those who exert themselves will not only develop their abilities but will also discover new skills they didn't previously possess.
examples.speaker: Jennings

examples.text: Many are stunted in their spiritual growth, in their ability to love, simply by failing to exercise their God-given ability to reason and think.
examples.speaker: Jennings

examples.text: This parable beautifully describes the law of exertion! What happens if you don’t use the talents you possess – if you don’t use it, you lose it. But if you apply yourself, you gain more abilities. No jury, no presentation of evidence, no judge passing sentence – it is the reality of the outcome of our choices.
examples.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: But the solid food of truth is for the mature, who, by constant use, have trained their faculties to distinguish true from false, good from evil, healthy from unhealthy.
for everyone who uses what they have will develop more. But whoever doesn't use what they have will lose it, for if you don't use it you lose it.

intro.text: By beholding we are changed. Jennings grounds this in neuroplasticity — the brain rewires toward whatever it admires — and in history: worship a God of love and you grow loving; worship a punishing dictator-god and you grow punitive. Choose an object of worship below and see the trajectory.

statement.text: One of God's design laws is the law of worship—by beholding we are changed. We actually become like the God we admire and worship. In psychiatry, this is known as modeling. … worship a God of love and become more loving; worship an authoritarian god and become more abusive.
statement.speaker: Jennings

statement.text: Law of worship: by beholding we are changed; also known as modeling. It is the principle that we become like whatever we spend time admiring, valuing, thinking about, worshiping, or esteeming.
statement.speaker: Jennings

We cannot have health in lies, in falsehood, out of harmony with truth and reality. … Thus, love always operates with the truth, speaks truth, applies truth, moves forward in the truth, for the truth heals and sets free (John 8:32).

Then you will experience the healing power of the truth, and the truth will set your entire being free."

intro.text: Come and Reason also issues the design-laws teaching as a three-page printed tract. Its text repeats the 2019 blog post almost word for word — the same 17 laws in the same order — and its opening paragraph restates the post’s gravity illustration (the 500-foot building and the 5-inch curb) in slightly different wording. The tract’s wording is quoted below.

opening.text: For instance, if you jump off a 500-foot building, you will die; step off a 5-inch curb and you might twist an ankle — the law of gravity doesn’t care and doesn’t change, but the degree of the violation causes a different degree of injury. Design laws always have a natural consequence; they do not require an external agent to punish someone who violates them.
opening.speaker: Jennings

title.text: Survival of the fittest vs the Circle of Giving

intro.text: Jennings reads the Fall as a change of operating principle: fear and selfishness, the drive to look out for me first, replaced the other-centered giving that life was built to run on. The Remedy makes this contrast explicit, naming the world's principle 'survival-of-the-fittest' and God's principle 'I love you so much that I will give my life in order that you might live'.

jennings.text: Fear and selfishness are commonly known in the world today as "survival of the fittest," or the drive to survive, or "kill or be killed," or "watch out for me first." It is the polar opposite of giving, love or beneficence, and it is the infection that is destroying God's creation.
jennings.speaker: Jennings

jennings.text: Because of God's intercession, there are now two antagonistic principles at war on planet Earth—love and survival of the fittest. … Such godly love is at war with the survival-of-the-fittest principle, which says, "I love myself so much I will do whatever I have to in order to protect, advance and exalt myself including, if necessary, killing you that I might live." Give my life that you might live, or kill you that I might live.
jennings.speaker: Jennings

jennings.text: The problem in the world today is that selfishness is so deeply wired into our system that scientists and many professed Christians purport this drive to survive is “natural” or “normal.” But the reality is the “survival of the fittest” instinct is Satan’s selfish infection of God’s creation which causes all nature to suffer (Romans 8:22).
jennings.speaker: Jennings

jennings.text: My view is that God designed human beings to love, with only altruistic motives for relationship, connection, and mutually uplifting beneficence. He designed us to promote the welfare of others without the knowledge or experience of fear and selfish concern. But Adam and Eve’s choice to believe lies about God broke their bonds of love and trust and caused them to become motivated by fear and selfishness, the survival-of-the-fittest drives.
jennings.speaker: Jennings

verses.remedy: He died to provide Remedy to all humanity so that those who live will not live dominated by selfishness, but in love for him who died to heal them and was raised again!
verses.why: he died so that the living no longer live dominated by selfishness but in love

verses.remedy: The old me who lived for self–who sought to get instead of give, the me who lived on the survival-of-the-fittest principle–died when I recognized the true significance of all that Christ has done. That old me no longer lives, but Christ–with his character of self-sacrificing love–now lives in me. The life I now live in this body I live by trust in the Son of God, who loved me and freely gave himself to win me back to trust and to purge humanity from selfishness and death.
verses.why: the old me who sought to get instead of give died; Christ's self-sacrificing character lives

verses.remedy: But if you instead practice the principle of survival of the fittest and attack and destroy others in order to promote yourselves, you will only experience ruin and death.
verses.why: attack and destroy others to promote yourself and reap only ruin and death

verses.remedy: The one who indulges the selfish nature will experience the natural consequences of a damaged mind — increased fear, broken relationships, separation from God, and eventual death; but the one who chooses to follow the Spirit, from the Spirit they will experience a healed mind, internal peace, unity with God, and eternal life.
verses.why: indulge the selfish nature and reap death; follow the Spirit and reap a healed mind

verses.remedy: in which you used to live when you followed the survival-of-the-fittest principle of the world instituted by the ruler of the kingdom of the air–the intelligent being whose principles are now at work in all those who reject truth, love, and freedom.
verses.why: the survival-of-the-fittest principle of the world was instituted by Satan

verses.remedy: All of us also were born infected with this destructive survival-of-the-fittest principle and at one time gratified its selfish and unhealthy desires and thoughts. Like the rest of humanity, we were born infected with this principle which — if not removed — would result in our self-destruction.
verses.why: all of us were born infected with this destructive principle

verses.remedy: You were taught that the former ways of life–the survival-of-the-fittest ways, the selfish me-first ways–only lead to self-destruction and death, and that health and life consist of putting off such motives and desires.
verses.why: the former selfish me-first ways lead only to self-destruction

verses.remedy: Don't do anything for selfish reasons or seek to promote yourself ahead of others, but in humbleness and love be more concerned for the welfare and good of others than for your own.
verses.why: do nothing for selfish reasons; be more concerned for others' good than your own

verses.remedy: Each one of you should not only be concerned with your own health and growth, but also work to help others become the healthiest Christians they can be.
verses.why: look beyond your own growth to help others become healthy

verses.remedy: For he has rescued us from the dominance of selfishness and survival-of-the-fittest methods that darken the mind and lead only to death, and has brought us into the kingdom of truth, righteousness, and self-sacrificing love — the kingdom of the Son he loves
verses.why: rescued from the dominance of survival-of-the-fittest methods into the kingdom of self-sacrificing love

verses.remedy: For selfishness, envy, and all violations of God's law of love break his design for life and cause chaos, disease, suffering, and everything evil.
verses.why: selfishness and envy break God's design and cause chaos, disease and everything evil

verses.remedy: Why is there so much hostility, fighting and arguments among you? Because the survival-of-the-fittest instinct controls you:
verses.why: fights and quarrels come because the survival-of-the-fittest instinct controls you

verses.remedy: if you want something but don't get it, you are willing to kill. You are selfish, coveting what you cannot have, constantly fighting, trying to get for yourselves. You do not obtain, because you do not seek God.
verses.why: wanting and not getting, willing to kill; constantly trying to get for yourselves

verses.remedy: And when you finally do ask God — because your motives are selfish, because you focus only on self-gratification — you don't get what you're asking for, because God doesn't use his power to supply you with means to further damage yourselves.
verses.why: selfish motives in prayer; God will not fund self-damage

verses.remedy: Anyone who hates another is a murderer, as murder happens in the mind and heart before it is carried out in action. You know that murder is the end result of the survival-of-the-fittest principle, and no one who remains infected with this self-first principle has God's eternal life recreated within them.
verses.why: murder is the end result of the survival-of-the-fittest principle

verses.remedy: This is how we know what love is: Jesus Christ voluntarily laid his life down for us. And we, who have been restored to Godlike love, will also give all we have, including laying down our lives for our brothers and sisters.
verses.why: love defined: Jesus laid his life down, and the restored will give all for others

verses.remedy: They overcame him by partaking of the Remedy–the perfect character of Christ the Lamb, symbolized by his blood–and by the evidence of their self-sacrificing lives, as they no longer loved their own selves so much as to shrink from death: they were healed to love just like Jesus.
verses.why: the overcomers no longer loved themselves so much as to shrink from death

pruned_note.text: Keyword scan of remedy_verses.json: 62 verses matched the narrow terms (survival, fittest, me-first/self-first, lose or save your life, greater love, hoard, look out for), plus 871 containing 'selfish' and 24 pairing give with receive. Each narrow hit was read; 41 verses were kept that plainly voice one of the two principles, the rest were pruned as narrative, duplicate renderings, or only incidental mentions of selfishness.

title.text: Which principle am I running on?

pairs.survival: I keep what I earn; nobody looks after me if I don't.
pairs.giving: What I have is in circulation; I give because that is how I was built to live.

pairs.survival: My hours are mine to protect; interruptions are threats.
pairs.giving: My time is a gift I can spend on someone else's good.

pairs.survival: When challenged, I win the argument or I lose standing.
pairs.giving: When challenged, I want what is actually true and good for us both, even if I lose.

pairs.survival: I need recognition, and someone else's credit feels like my loss.
pairs.giving: Another person's success is something I can celebrate without keeping score.

pairs.survival: Letting it go would make me weak; they owe me.
pairs.giving: I release the debt because love does not keep a record of wrongs.

pairs.survival: If I stop working, I fall behind and lose ground.
pairs.giving: I can rest because my life does not depend on my own striving.

pairs.survival: I must secure myself first; then I can think about others.
pairs.giving: Trusting God's care frees me to attend to others without anxiety.

pairs.survival: Success means getting ahead of others.
pairs.giving: Success means others are healthier and freer because I was there.

pairs.survival: I shade the truth when honesty would cost me.
pairs.giving: I tell the truth even when it costs me, because love and truth go together.

pairs.survival: I love those who are useful to me and protect me.
pairs.giving: I love people for their good, including those who can give nothing back.

scoring.intro: For each theme, pick the statement that is closer to how you actually think when nobody is watching. Count how many fall on each side.
scoring.mostly_survival: Mostly survival. The me-first instinct is steering; Jennings would say this is the inherited condition, not a verdict, and that it changes as truth about God is believed and trust returns.
scoring.mixed: Mixed. Both principles are active, which is what Jennings describes as the war in every heart; notice which themes still run on fear and bring those to God for healing.
scoring.mostly_giving: Mostly giving. The law of love is increasingly the motive; keep beholding Christ so that other-centered love continues to displace what remains of fear.

jennings_on_change.text: It is truth about God that destroys lies and wins us back to trust. In trust we open our hearts and experience God's love, which overcome fear and enable us to give rather than constantly seek to get. This is conversion, the experience of a fundamental switch in the primary motive of the heart—from our inherent survival-of-the-fittest selfishness to other-centered love.
jennings_on_change.speaker: Jennings

jennings_on_change.text: So all who accept Christ open their heart/mind in trust and the Holy Spirit comes and recreates in them a new heart and right spirit, restoring God’s law of love again into humanity (Psalms 51:5). This is the new convenant, “I will write my law on your hearts and minds” (Heb 8:10). This is only possible because of what Christ achieved at Calvary.
jennings_on_change.speaker: Jennings

kept.text: Keep giving and the circle keeps turning: breath, water, pollen, time, attention, and the life that depends on them all keep flowing back to you.

broken.text: Hoard what you were built to give and the circle closes on you; whatever stops giving begins, by that very act, to die.

jennings.text: But life itself is built upon the law of love. Love is the principle of giving, and all living organisms operate upon it. With every breath, an exhale and inhale, you give away carbon dioxide (CO2) to the plants and the plants give oxygen back to you. If you put a plastic bag over your head and “hoard” your CO2 for yourself, then you will die. Everything that lives gives. Cease to give and one dies.
jennings.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: And thus we have been genuinely transformed from beings motivated and driven by selfishness to fully healed children of God, motivated and energized by the love God has for us. God is love, and those who live a life of love live in unity and oneness with God–and God with them.

kept.text: Leave people genuinely free to agree, disagree, stay or go, and love, trust and individuality have the room they need to grow.

broken.text: Coerce someone and three things follow on their own: their love for you is damaged, a desire to rebel is planted, and if they stay their individuality slowly erodes.

jennings.text: The Law of Liberty, one of God’s natural design laws, reveals that love only grows in an atmosphere of freedom. If you violate that freedom and coerce another, love is damaged and a desire to rebel is instilled. If freedom isn’t restored, individuality erodes and those who stay become mindless followers.
jennings.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: We experience Jesus through the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom from confusion, fear, and selfishness.

kept.text: Spend your attention on a God of love and your brain rewires toward love; you gradually become like the One you admire.

broken.text: Fix your admiration on a punishing, authoritarian or degraded object and you become harder, more fearful and more like it, no sentence required.

jennings.text: One of God's design laws is the law of worship—by beholding we are changed. We actually become like the God we admire and worship. In psychiatry, this is known as modeling. … We were constructed by God to adapt and change based on the choices we make: worship a God of love and become more loving; worship an authoritarian god and become more abusive.
jennings.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: Those who make them will become like them, as will all who worship and trust in them.

kept.text: Exercise a muscle, a skill or a faculty of judgment and it grows stronger with use.

broken.text: Leave an ability idle and it weakens and finally disappears; nobody takes it from you, it simply atrophies.

jennings.text: This parable beautifully describes the law of exertion! What happens if you don’t use the talents you possess – if you don’t use it, you lose it. But if you apply yourself, you gain more abilities. No jury, no presentation of evidence, no judge passing sentence – it is the reality of the outcome of our choices.
jennings.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: But the solid food of truth is for the mature, who, by constant use, have trained their faculties to distinguish true from false, good from evil, healthy from unhealthy.

kept.text: Build, fly, cook and walk in harmony with gravity, motion and thermodynamics and the material world is reliable and safe to live in.

broken.text: Step off a height or ignore friction and inertia and the damage arrives by itself, scaled to how far you departed from the law.

jennings.text: He sustains the laws of physics and the laws of health upon which life operates and in this way, God is involved. But, God does not cause the defects in His creation. Those occur simply because human beings have broken His design …
jennings.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: He existed before anything, and it is he who holds all things together.

kept.text: Reason from what is actually true and your sums, bridges and conclusions hold up under anyone's scrutiny.

broken.text: Insist that 2 + 2 is whatever an authority says and reality does not change, but you become easy prey for the next, louder authority.

jennings.text: If you believe 2+2=4 merely becausethe teacher says so—you may know the right answer, but you are not secure in reality. All a deceiver has to do is be more persuasive, convincing, dynamic, or come from a position of higher authority than the teacher and tell you 2+2=7, and you will believe it.
jennings.speaker: Jennings

kept.text: Breathe clean air, eat, drink, move, rest and avoid toxins as the body was designed to, and health is the normal result.

broken.text: Smoke, starve, or stop breathing and no one has to impose cancer, weakness or suffocation; the violation carries its own result.

jennings.text: Think of God’s law like “the laws of health.” If someone violates the laws of health does anyone have to “impose” penalties on them such as illness, pain, suffering, and/or death? For example, take a person who smokes. Does anyone (including God) have to impose the penalty of cancer or emphysema?
jennings.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: Dear friend, I pray that all things are well with you, that your health is good, and your mind is sharp, clear and at peace.

kept.text: Spend yourself, then rest and recover, and you are able to spend again, often with more than before.

broken.text: Keep drawing on a resource without letting it recover and you burn out, injure yourself and end up unable to give at all.

jennings.text: One of Satan’s traps, if he cannot get good people to choose evil, is to overwhelm them with so many worthy and good projects, responsibilities, and duties that they forget to love themselves; they stop resting and overwork themselves doing good to the point that they burn out and are no longer useful in God’s cause. Thus, they have not loved themselves by giving what they need in order to stay healthy.
jennings.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: After giving them a moment to think, he said, "The Sabbath was created as a gift for humanity — to be a blessing for human beings. Human beings were not created as a gift for the Sabbath.

sowing.name: The law of sowing and reaping

kept.text: Sow truth, healthy habits and your own hard thinking and you harvest character, health and judgment you actually own.

broken.text: Sow lies, indulgence or borrowed answers and you reap exactly that crop; nobody has to add a penalty to the harvest.

jennings.text: The law of sowing and reaping is: We reap what we sow. If we sow seeds that violate what is true, what is healthy, that is contrary to what is good, that violates the very protocols of life and health that the Creator built into our universe, then we will reap destruction. Paul in Galatians writes, “The one who sows to please his sinful nature, from that nature will reap destruction” (6:8 NIV84).
jennings.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: But don't delude yourselves: God cannot be tricked or fooled, and his methods cannot be evaded. A person actually reaps what they sow; a person actually receives the results of their own choices.

love_over_fear.name: The law of love overcoming fear

kept.text: Let love for another fire and it calms your own fear circuitry, freeing you to act for them even at cost to yourself.

broken.text: Starve the love circuits and fear runs unchecked, shrinking your world to self-protection and raising the risk of despair.

jennings.text: Neuroscience demonstrates that when the brain’s love circuits activate, they calm the fear/stress circuits. Activities and experiences that increase love, altruism, other-centered connection, and meaning will decrease suicide risk, whereas actions that isolate and increase fear will increase suicide risk.
jennings.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: In love, there is no fear. Fear is part of the infection of selfishness, but is purged by love, as fear has to do with concern for oneself. The one who remains self-focused and afraid has not been healed by God’s love.

fear_damages_love.name: The law of fear damaging love and inciting selfishness

kept.text: Keep fear in its place through trust and you stay able to notice and care for the people around you.

broken.text: Let fear take the driver's seat and concern for others drains away; you hide, flee or shove past them to save yourself.

jennings.text: Fear is part of the infection of sin and is the feeling that results from broken trust. Fear causes selfishness. Fearful, self-centered decision-making is the opposite of love; it leads us to seek to save ourselves, to move away from trusting in God with one’s life and from acting in selfless love for others.
jennings.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: Adam answered, “I heard you in the garden and I was afraid, because I was naked; so I hid.”

forgiveness.name: The law of forgiveness versus resentment

kept.text: Forgive the one who wronged you and your own heart and mind are released to heal, whatever the offender does.

broken.text: Hold the grudge and it is you who carries the toxic stress, inflammation and bitterness everywhere you go.

jennings.text: Grudge holding, bitterness, resentment are toxic emotions that activate the brain’s stress pathways causing activation of inflammatory factors. Failure to resolve such feelings results in increased oxidative stress and damage to physical, mental and relational health. Forgiving those who have offended us does not mean what they did was okay, but relieves us of carrying the toxic emotions of anger and resentment everywhere we go and over time ruining our own health.
jennings.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: Be kind, gentle, compassionate and forgiving with each other as God is forgiving to you; remember that all humanity suffers with the same infection of selfishness, and God provides the same Remedy for all.

kept.text: Face the truth about yourself now and it displaces lies, frees you from fear and sets you on the path to healing.

broken.text: Deny, project and delay and the truth still waits for you; it only arrives later, harder, and to a mind less able to bear it.

jennings.text: There is a truth I tell my patients, “You can never avoid the truth. You can only delay the day you deal with the truth.” … Or we can delay dealing with the truth, put it off, deny, externalize, project, blame, and scapegoat others, but if we don’t deal with the truth now, one day when Christ comes back each person will then come face to face with ultimate truth.
jennings.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: Then you will experience the healing power of the truth, and the truth will set your entire being free."

kept.text: Value God's principles in your heart and your words and actions reveal them without any effort at image management.

broken.text: Whatever you actually love leaks out in what you say and do; a heart full of the world's methods cannot hide it for long.

jennings.text: Jesus said, “For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks” (Matthew 12:34 NKJV). People reveal their own views and ideas by what they say and do.
jennings.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: The good person speaks and does good out of the wellspring of good stored within them, and the evil person speaks and does evil out of the wellspring of evil stored within them. So, speaking against the Holy Spirit reveals that one's heart is closed to the working of the Spirit.

kept.text: Pursue health in body, mind, relationships and spirit and happiness arrives as the by-product.

broken.text: Chase pleasure instead of health and you trade a moment's relief for the sickness, conflict and guilt that make happiness impossible.

jennings.text: Happiness is the byproduct of healthiness in all domains—physical, mental, emotional, relational, and spiritual. When we are physically ill, we are not happy; mental or emotional illness—not happy; relationship conflict—not happy; spiritual sickness (guilt, shame, condemnation)—not happy.
jennings.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: But those who examine themselves honestly in the light of God's law of love–the law that heals and frees from fear and selfishness–and continue to do this daily, not ignoring what is learned but applying it diligently, experience happiness as they are healed and transformed.

kept.text: Accept that healing hurts, choose the treatment that heals rather than the one that hurts least, and recovery becomes possible.

broken.text: Spend your life on pain relief instead of healing and the wound never closes; you only get worse while avoiding the discomfort.

jennings.text: Once there is brokenness, woundedness, or injury of any kind—there are no pain-free options! The only options we have after we are wounded are to heal or not heal, but the path of healing, whether setting a bone, cleaning dirt out of an abrasion, or resolving trauma issues, is accompanied by pain and discomfort. If we choose only that which hurts the least and feels the best in the moment, then we persistently choose to avoid healing and things will get worse.
jennings.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: The sacrifice you desire is a humble and teachable attitude; a broken and repentant heart

sin_death.name: The law of sin and death

kept.text: There is no keeping this one; it is the anti-law, and life is found only by being healed out of it back into love.

broken.text: Live by survival of the fittest, saving self at others' expense, and the predictable results follow: fear, pain, broken relationships and finally death.

jennings.text: The law of sin and death is the survival-of-the-fittest motive driven by fear and the need to protect self—especially at the expense of others. It is doing whatever one needs to do to survive, even if that means killing others to save self.
jennings.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: For the infection of selfishness leads only to death, but the gift of God is eternal life through the healing Remedy procured by Jesus Christ our Lord.

intro.text: Jennings' favourite test case. Gravity never changes and never punishes; what changes is how far you step out of harmony with it. Slide the height and watch the consequence scale while the law stays exactly the same.

quotes.text: The only variables would be in the damage that results with various degrees of violating a law. For instance, jump off a 500-foot building and you die; step off a 5-inch curb and you twist an ankle — the law of gravity doesn’t change, but the degree of the violation causes a different degree of injury (note that these laws have a natural consequence; they do not require an external agent to punish someone who violates these laws).
quotes.speaker: Jennings

quotes.text: For example, the law of gravity is a design law upon which nature is created to operate. If you jump off a building God doesn’t have to inflict a penalty, the penalty is inherent, that is, you will most likely die upon impact with the ground.
quotes.speaker: Jennings

quotes.text: For instance gravity is a natural law. When we transgress natural law there is no need for an imposed punishment, because the penalty is inherent. If you jump off a bridge, then God does not need to send an angel to break your legs when you hit the ground below.
quotes.speaker: Jennings

gloss.text: Minor departure, minor injury; a day of limping.
Same law, slightly more height, noticeably more damage.
Weeks in plaster; the consequence now demands real healing.
Survival is the rare exception; the body cannot absorb this violation.
Nobody has to be sent to inflict anything; the outcome is inherent in the fall.

steps_note.text: Heights and labels are illustrative, written for the slider; Jennings himself names only the 5-inch curb and the 500-foot building.

objection.text: "Design law" is just natural law with a religious label. If gravity and the laws of health run by themselves, where is God in any of this?

reply.text: Thus, God is in control of what God controls — and God controls Himself and all His laws. He sustains reality; He keeps the universe running upon the protocols and laws He established.
reply.speaker: Jennings

reply.text: Why are men without excuse? It is because they have been given the Ten Commandments or other Scripture? No! It is because God’s invisible qualities and divine nature are clearly seen from what has been made, from nature, from the design laws our Creator has built into the operations of reality!
reply.speaker: Jennings

strength_note.text: Jennings answers from inside the frame: God is the one who built and sustains the protocols, and Romans 1:20 says the laws themselves reveal Him. That is coherent, but it is a theological claim rather than an argument a naturalist would feel forced to accept; his nearest independent evidence is the fine-tuning passage he borrows from Nancy Pearcey in the 2019 post.

objection.text: The Ten Commandments are literally commands, thundered from Sinai and written in stone. Surely that is God imposing law.

reply.text: Sinful mankind did not comprehend this reality, so God stepped in with a stop-gap measure to help us in two ways. First, the10 Commandments were added, because we needed them to help diagnose how sick we are. And second, they were added to protect us from ourselves and lead us to Christ. Just like a parental rule not to smoke protects the child from harming themselves, the 10 Commandments were “distilled” out of the Law of Love to protect us.
reply.speaker: Jennings

reply.text: My point is that verbal commands, edicts, and directives cannot achieve morality. Morality cannot be enforced through imposed law and external law enforcement. To attempt to do this actually causes more sin, more rebellion, more immorality. EGW put it this way:
reply.speaker: Jennings

strength_note.text: This is the best-developed reply in the corpus. Jennings grants that God gives verbal commands, then distinguishes the written code (added after sin, a diagnostic distillation for immature minds) from the eternal law it describes, and backs it with Galatians 3:19, Romans 5:20 and a long line of Ellen White statements. The weak point is only that his opponents read the same texts the other way.

objection.text: If sin destroys the sinner all by itself, with no sentence from God, then God is not actually needed to forgive anyone. Forgiveness drops out of the picture.

reply.text: God is love and therefore God’s heart is always one of forgiveness, and never needs inducement or requests to be so. Our confession and request to be forgiven is the opening of the heart to receive the forgiveness that God constantly extends.
reply.speaker: Jennings

reply.text: Jesus came because God forgives and because God’s forgiveness, extended freely from His heart, is notsufficient to save us from sin. Why? Because God was never the barrier to salvation; sin in us is the barrier.
reply.speaker: Jennings

strength_note.text: Jennings largely agrees with the premise and turns it: God's forgiveness is never in doubt and never the obstacle, which is exactly why forgiveness alone cannot save. What is needed is healing of the heart and mind, and that is what Christ provides. The reply is internally consistent; critics will say it quietly redefines forgiveness rather than answering the charge.

objection.text: Whatever you say about love and liberty, the Sabbath is plainly an arbitrary rule. Nothing in nature says the seventh day; it only matters because God said so.

reply.text: Thus, after six days of creation, God created a day of freedom, a day where God stops using power and steps back, giving His creatures space and time to consider and think. Day seven is the only day that reveals the character of the One who wields the power: God presented evidence (truth), in love, and left His creatures free to decide for themselves. No coercion, no intimidation, no pressure, just freedom!
reply.speaker: Jennings

reply.text: The Sabbath is a day of rest by its creation; it was made by God for this purpose at the end of creation week. The Sabbath is an evidence of design-law — truth, presented in love, while leaving others free — and is a sign of God’s method of governing.
reply.speaker: Jennings

strength_note.text: Jennings relocates the Sabbath from rule to evidence: a built-in weekly reminder of how God governs (truth, love, freedom), tied to the creation-week narrative and to his Great Controversy backstory. The move is attractive, but it leans on his reading of the Hebrew "it" as "yourself" and on a backstory that non-Adventists will not share; it does not show that the seventh day as such has inherent consequences.

objection.text: Ellen White repeatedly speaks of God's law as the law of His government, with transgression, penalties and the wrath of God against sin. That sounds like imposed law from an Adventist prophet.

reply.text: What do you understand God’s wrath to be? Romans 1:18–32 and many other passages define God’s wrath as letting sinners go to reap what sin causes; it is when God stops using power to protect, restrain, and hold at bay what sin causes. Human law, however, defines wrath as the use of power to inflict punishment for rule-breaking. We will be misled in our understanding if we use this sin-marred human understanding rather than a biblical definition of wrath.
reply.speaker: Jennings

reply.text: Thus, the entire description by this author is a description of reality, of design law, and there is nothing penal/legal going on in the plan of salvation. It is entirely the outworking of truth and love in an atmosphere of freedom!
reply.speaker: Jennings

supporting.text: We are not to regard God as waiting to punish the sinner for his sin. The sinner brings the punishment upon himself. His own actions start a train of circumstances that bring the sure result. Every act of transgression reacts upon the sinner, works in him a change of character, and makes it more easy for him to transgress again. By choosing to sin, men separate themselves from God, cut themselves off from the channel of blessing, and the sure result is ruin and death
supporting.speaker: Ellen G. White

strength_note.text: Jennings' strategy is to read Ellen White widely, define wrath biblically as God letting go, and show that her own context speaks of cleansing and healing. He can quote her saying the sinner brings the punishment on himself, which is strong support. But the corpus never engages the specific phrase "law of His government" head-on, and the penal-sounding sentences are reinterpreted rather than refuted; the reply convinces those who already accept his lens.

objection.text: An Adventist pastor's pushback: love, liberty and worship are biblical virtues, not laws. Scripture presents God's law as commanded, covenantal and judicial; your model swaps biblical categories for natural-law philosophy and therapy.

reply.text: Do you not realize that “principles” is another word for “laws” when the laws are design laws?
reply.speaker: Jennings

reply.text: The truth is that there is not one imposed law in God’s kingdom; that is why Jesus said His kingdom is not of this world, because all worldly kingdoms operate upon imposed law with imposed punishments. Remember, Jesus said this when Israel and the temple with all the imposed laws were still on the earth. Jesus didn’t say, “My kingdom is not of this world—except for Israel, that is how my kingdom works.”
reply.speaker: Jennings

strength_note.text: Jennings is strongest where he marshals Ellen White's language of "principles" transgressed before any written law existed, and where he insists that believing in an imposed-law god changes the believer. He is weakest when he tells the pastor his mind is "ensnared in the imposed-law lie": that is a diagnosis, not an argument, and the pastor's exegetical point about covenant and judgment is met mainly by redefinition and a referral to another blog.

meaning.text: A principle or protocol upon which reality is actually built to operate (gravity, respiration, love). It is testable and unchanging, and breaking it damages the breaker without anyone having to add a penalty.

quote.text: Natural Law being the principles or protocols upon which life is based, like the law of respiration, or gravity, or thermodynamics. Imposed law would be rules put in force by an external authority, such as tax law, speed limits, parking regulations etc.
quote.speaker: Jennings

meaning.text: A made-up rule with no inherent consequence (speed limits, tax codes), which therefore has to be enforced by an external authority through threatened or inflicted punishment. Jennings' claim is that Christianity after Constantine began reading God's law this way.

quote.text: Human beings cannot create reality, so we make up rules, without inherent consequence (speed limits, tax laws, littering, etc.), and then enforce those laws with threats of inflicted punishment (fines, imprisonment, death penalty).
quote.speaker: Jennings

meaning.text: Jennings' preferred synonym for design law: the construction specification the Creator built the universe and life to run on, as opposed to a regulation issued to govern it.

quote.text: When God built His universe, He constructed it to operate in harmony with His nature and character. The construction protocol upon which the universe is built is commonly known as God’s law.
quote.speaker: Jennings

meaning.text: The picture Jennings uses for the law of love in nature: breath exchanged with plants, water cycling from ocean to cloud to river, pollen for pollination. Life continues only while the circle of giving is unbroken.

quote.text: If you break this law, this circle of giving, by tying a plastic bag over your head and selfishly hoarding your body’s CO2, you break the design protocol for life—and the result is death. … This circle of giving is the law that God constructed life to operate upon.
quote.speaker: Jennings

meaning.text: Jennings' name for the law of sin and death: the fear-driven, me-first principle that infected humanity at the fall. The exact opposite of the law of love, and the thing Christ came to destroy in human nature.

quote.text: Fear and selfishness are commonly known in the world today as "survival of the fittest," or the drive to survive, or "kill or be killed," or "watch out for me first." It is the polar opposite of giving, love or beneficence, and it is the infection that is destroying God's creation.
quote.speaker: Jennings

meaning.text: Love exists only in an atmosphere of freedom. Violate someone's liberty and love is damaged, rebellion is incited, and individuality erodes; this is why God will not coerce even to save.

quote.text: Love exists only in an atmosphere of freedom. Thus, as the Bible teaches, “The Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom (2 Corinthians 3:17 NIV84). This is the law of liberty, a design law that governs the operations of hearts and minds. Individuality, development, love, and growth occur only in freedom.
quote.speaker: Jennings

meaning.text: Also called modeling. We are changed, neurobiologically and in character, to become like whatever we admire, worship and dwell on. The character of the God you worship therefore matters more than the name.

quote.text: Law of worship: by beholding we are changed; also known as modeling. It is the principle that we become like whatever we spend time admiring, valuing, thinking about, worshiping, or esteeming.
quote.speaker: Jennings

meaning.text: The result that follows from violating a design law by itself, as death follows from suffocation. In Jennings' reading, "the wages of sin is death" names an inherent consequence, not a sentence handed down by God.

quote.text: What I do say is that the penalty is not an external, God-imposed legal sentence, but an inherent consequence (“penalty “) that comes from sin itself.
quote.speaker: Jennings
